# Shaman regional research and bounded design review

## Status and assignment

This is a planning proposal from `chaosx_improvement_loop_planner` for parent review.
It is not an accepted specification, an implementation claim, or a catalog change.
The requested package uses Event 118, while the supplied catalog records Shaman as 129 and Plague of locust as 118.
The parent owns that identity reconciliation and runtime investigation.
The parent also owns final acceptance, exact state mapping, probability audit, Event 013 integration, asset prompts, packaging, and durable delivery.
This handoff changes only this planning document.

The team source gate is already complete according to `source_review/complete_source_coverage.json`.
This assignment continued that reviewed task rather than reopening source ingestion.
The canonical planner role, current AGENTS, the supplied task brief, improvement-loop guidance, event-planning guidance, text-direction reference, and relevant event, decision, asset, portrait, and subagent guidance informed this proposal.
The older preliminary-ingestion language in `source_review/task_state.md` does not supersede the parent's explicit passed-gate instruction.

Every invented structural term in this document is a working label, not final localisation.
The regional identifiers R1 through R6 are research identifiers, not player-facing titles.
Real practitioner terms and geographic names are source facts rather than invented route names.
The document gives direction only and contains no proposed player prose, option wording, quotations, implementation code, generated art, or live-game claims.

## Recommendation

Accept a finite roster of six authored regional profiles, subject to the specific map and period-presentation limits below.
Use Olkhon and the western Baikal shore, the Podkamennaya Tunguska basin, Jeju, the lower Kuskokwim and adjoining Yukon delta, the Luang Prabang uplands, and a Tày community in the Cao Bằng uplands.
These profiles support different local food systems, routes, hazards, and defensive preparation without introducing additional religious factions or national systems.
The roster naturally accommodates several possible major-country controllers, but no major power is guaranteed an eligible home region.
Campaign conquest can change the recipient without changing the community's identity.

Keep one government-selected rite, the two requested aid purposes, peaceful refusal, persecution with conditional local unrest, outcome uncertainty, and the single True Sight evolution at Chaos 400 or above.
Add depth through a material commitment, a local consequence, remembered treatment, and one bounded aftercare opportunity.
Stop expansion there.
Six cultures do not justify six separate progression systems.

## Evidence rules and cultural boundaries

The source register at the end lists only pages actually opened and read for claims used here.
Search snippets, blocked pages, inaccessible downloads, and unseen video contents do not count as evidence.
Where an article was only partly accessible, the register identifies the consulted portion.
Modern fieldwork can establish a title, community, place, or documented practice, but does not establish that a modern photograph reproduces 1936 clothing or that every village had an identical tradition.
The proposed 1936 to 1945 visitor is fictional and anonymous.
No cited ethnographic participant becomes the visitor's historical identity.

The umbrella event concept does not make these traditions interchangeable.
Jeju simbang, Hmong txiv neeb, Tày Then practitioners, Yup'ik angalkut, Buryat practitioners, and Evenki saman retain distinct geographic and cultural contexts.
Do not substitute a neighboring people's title, costume, ritual instrument, sacred image, song, or cosmology because it looks recognizable.
Do not turn terms for different kinds of practitioners into good and evil classes.
Do not infer a uniform gender restriction from one local sample.
Do not interpret a religious account of healing, weather control, or prediction as empirical evidence of supernatural efficacy.

The culture selector must never alter the base probability of fraud, practical expertise, genuine supernatural ability, spectacular success, or malicious intent.
Local geography may determine which material preparation makes sense and how a real threat causes harm.
Those environmental effects must remain separate from the hidden explanation for the visitor's abilities.

This research does not approve any sacred image, object, song, or text as an asset.
The art recommendation uses anonymous people doing practical local work within a fictional event scene.
It does not require a recruitable character or a separate portrait.
If a later accepted requirement creates a grounded portrait, use the current source-first portrait pipeline and an attributed real subject or authentic institutional source.
Do not generate a plausible historical indigenous officeholder to bypass that gate.

## Home region and controller contract

Each profile has a cultural home boundary and must later receive a separate, verified game-map boundary.
The cultural boundary is not permission to describe a much larger game state as culturally homogeneous.
A state containing several communities can host one local visitor without making that visitor representative of everyone in the state.

The parent should resolve each profile to one named home state or a tightly bounded state group that the runtime can actually support.
The entry recipient must be a major country that directly controls the chosen home state at selection and at acceptance.
Ownership, faction membership, military access, or control through a subject is insufficient by itself.
If the map cannot represent a coherent local effect without covering a much larger and unrelated area, omit that profile from the launch roster or narrow its effect through a verified supported scope.
Do not create new states or countries simply to preserve the proposed count.

Examples of controller interaction below are conditional campaign situations.
They are not assertions about the current repository's 1936 state ownership or scripting support.
A visitor may cooperate with an outside government to protect the local population without endorsing that government's rule, ideology, religion, or military campaign.
The prose direction should preserve that distinction through the visitor's local purpose and the affected civilians.

Freeze the community and home region when the visit is accepted.
Changing the controller must not change a Yup'ik visitor into a different regional tradition or transfer paid benefits to an enemy.
The parent should prefer recipient selection followed by eligible regional selection so that adding more researched profiles does not silently increase one country's entry frequency.
Any actual weighting belongs in the probability audit.

## R1. Olkhon and the western shore of Lake Baikal

### Source facts and geographic boundary

Bound this profile to Olkhon Island and the immediately adjoining western Baikal communities in the Olkhon area of present-day Irkutsk Oblast.
Do not use all Siberia or all Buryatia as the cultural boundary.
Wierucka's original 2010 fieldwork documents local Buryat shamanic activity on Olkhon and distinguishes local needs from organized and visitor-facing practice [B1].
The Russian Museum of Ethnography separately documents Buryat shamanic and Buddhist material in its own collections [B2].

Use the English description Buryat shaman in the planning contract.
The term böö is attested in Balogh's original fieldwork among Buryats in Mongolia, but that source explicitly notes dialect influence [B3].
That establishes a related Buryat term and does not finish the local Olkhon terminology check.
If final localisation uses a native title, require a source tied to the selected Baikal community.

### Fictional gameplay direction

A major country controlling the home area can receive an offer aimed at local households and their food or transport needs.
Land aid should act on an existing local crisis first.
In calm conditions, use a substantial food-recovery or husbandry result suited to the chosen settlement and season, rather than assuming every Baikal community is a grain village.
Warrior guidance should concern local shore approaches, winter exposure, route choice, supply shelters, or prepared defensive positions within the verified home area.
Its strength should come from a short period of useful local preparation.

The controller's representative should be able to understand the proposal as a practical request for resources even when the visitor describes its purpose religiously.
No ideology receives an automatic persecution result.
The requested persecution consequence depends on the visitor's demonstrated local standing and the act committed.

### Visual and historical limits

Use a fictional scene with residents, supplies, and a locally appropriate lakeshore or settlement.
Do not combine a modern ceremonial costume, a generalized Mongolian antler headdress, Buddhist liturgical objects, and an invented spirit emblem.
Do not reproduce a sacred rock, ongon, shrine, or real ritual as a generic magical prop.
B1 is modern fieldwork with historical background, so a precise 1930s costume remains an asset-research task.
No claim is made that its modern organizations existed in the game period.

## R2. Evenki communities in the Podkamennaya Tunguska basin

### Source facts and geographic boundary

Use the Podkamennaya Tunguska basin in the middle Yenisei region, within the subarctic taiga studied by Ssorin-Chaikov.
Do not silently substitute the Lower Tunguska or the entire Evenki distribution.
His primary field and archival work describes local practice, the term saman, and Soviet-period change in this specific area [E1].
The Pitt Rivers Museum's community collaboration provides a separate regional comparison and historical collection context [E2].
Its Chirinda and Tura material must not be relabeled as Podkamennaya field evidence.

### Fictional gameplay direction

The visit should center on a small set of local settlements and travel routes even if a larger state is the mechanical host.
A controlling major government may welcome help because local guides and residents can identify where supplies are being lost or where travelers face exposure.
Calm land aid should concern hunting, fishing, herding, or stored food recovery as appropriate to the selected locality.
It should not produce a grain-harvest story in taiga communities by default.

Warrior guidance can make a temporary local supply route, shelter plan, crossing choice, or defensive approach valuable.
Requiring troops to remain in the named area supplies a real opportunity cost.
The benefit ends when they leave, when the commitment expires, or when the government loses the relevant authority.
No skill follows a division around the world as a permanent ethnic trait.

### Visual and historical limits

Use the source's taiga setting, ordinary work, and local travel as the scene's foundation.
An anonymous practitioner can be present without a close portrait or a prominently reconstructed sacred outfit.
The museum's late nineteenth or early twentieth century headdress record is one provenanced object, not a uniform for every Evenki practitioner [E3].
The archival study supports historical change and repression, but should not become a scripted instruction that a particular ideology must persecute the visitor.
Do not use colonial descriptions as a claim that the culture remained static.

## R3. Jeju coastal communities

### Source facts and geographic boundary

Use Jeju Island, with the community context anchored in Geonip-dong and the northeastern coast rather than all Korea.
The Jeju National University account published by ICHCAP uses simbang and describes a local ritual context concerned with fishing, sea safety, farming, and community welfare [J1].
It also identifies later shrine relocation, which prevents treating the current site layout as a game-period reconstruction.

### Fictional gameplay direction

If Japan or another major country directly controls the island, the visitor's request remains centered on island residents.
Acceptance should not declare Korean cultural consent to the controller's rule.
The same conditions must hold if a different major takes the island during the campaign.

Land aid in calm conditions should be able to improve local food availability through fishing and recovery of working capacity.
During a real crisis it can support relief already owned by the crisis system.
Weather exposure, the condition of local stores, and damage to routes are appropriate practical concerns.
Warrior guidance should affect only troops defending or moving through the home island area, using shelter, coastal approach knowledge, and local supply preparation.
It should not grant a national naval bonus or reveal distant fleets.

### Visual and historical limits

Use island residents moving supplies, repairing equipment, or preparing shelter with the visitor present in the scene.
The communal rite documented by J1 is seasonal and socially specific.
Do not rename the government's arbitrary aid choice as a reenactment of that rite.
Do not borrow its deity names, invocation text, ritual sequence, or current ceremonial wardrobe to imply authenticity for the fictional event.
Use simbang rather than treating the general Korean term mudang as sufficient local precision.
The final asset worker still needs period references for clothing, port structures, and boats.

## R4. Yup'ik communities of the lower Kuskokwim and adjoining Yukon delta

### Source facts and geographic boundary

Bound the profile to southwest Alaska, concentrating on the lower Kuskokwim coast and adjacent Yukon-Kuskokwim delta communities.
Do not extend it to all Alaska, all Inuit peoples, or the Aleutian chain.
The Calista community account uses angalkut for practitioners and describes remembered roles involving local welfare, food abundance, weather, and travel [Y1].
The bilingual community oral-history publication verifies the singular angalkuq and provides early twentieth century recollections [Y2].
ELOKA's work with Yup'ik elders documents place knowledge of rivers, sloughs, sandbars, and seasonal routes [Y3].

### Fictional gameplay direction

If the USA or another major directly controls the home area, local aid should respond to the needs of the delta communities.
Peaceful refusal leaves them alone and ends the visit.
Persecution should have a local consequence only when this particular visitor has credible community standing.
Do not present either Christianity or indigenous practice as a mandatory alignment for the entire population.

Calm land aid should concern fishing, hunting, food preservation, access to stores, or recovery after travel disruption.
It should not use a cereal-harvest visual or mechanically create farmland.
Warrior guidance can help troops sustain a temporary position through route knowledge, supply caching, shelter, and avoidance of exposed crossings.
The government must commit real supply resources or tie down troops in the named area to obtain the stronger effect.

### Visual and historical limits

Use an active settlement or travel scene with food stores, practical equipment, and people working.
Do not use an Iñupiaq, Alutiiq, Unangan, or Tlingit object as interchangeable decoration.
Do not reproduce ceremonial masks, songs, or spirit figures simply because they are documented in a collection.
Y2 records period memories, but does not establish that a named historical practitioner should be inserted into the event.
The modern place-name atlas establishes geographic knowledge, not a period radio or cartographic asset.

## R5. Hmong communities in the Luang Prabang uplands

### Source facts and geographic boundary

Use Hmong upland settlements in the Luang Prabang region, with Pouxang village as the research anchor rather than the whole of Laos.
The TAEC and PhotoForward community research project includes locally produced interviews and photographs about Hmong shamanic practice [H1].
An original interview project at Carleton records the term txiv neeb from Hmong practitioners and demonstrates variation between families [H2].
That interview is a diaspora source, so it corroborates the title without proving every detail for a 1930s Luang Prabang settlement.
The local tourism authority distinguishes Hmong upland rice cultivation from other regional communities' livelihoods [H3].

### Fictional gameplay direction

If France or another major directly controls the relevant home state, the offer should concern a local community's survival and routes.
Do not make the practitioner the ruler of a fictional hill federation or the voice of every upland population.
Government acceptance can fund practical supplies for local households without converting the community into an imperial recruitment pool.

Calm land aid can support an upland harvest, restoration of food stores, or recovery of damaged approaches.
An active local crisis takes precedence over generic prosperity.
Warrior guidance can concern foot routes, supply-carrying limits, sheltered positions, and defensive preparation near the home settlements.
The rite should not grant universal jungle warfare ability or call the Hmong interchangeable with Khmu, Iu Mien, Akha, or other nearby peoples.

### Visual and historical limits

Use a fictional hillside settlement and a practical collective task.
Do not combine every recognizable highland garment into one costume.
TAEC explicitly distinguishes Hmong clothing traditions, which makes a universal embroidered festival outfit an unsuitable shortcut [H4].
Do not reproduce the interview subjects' faces, individual ritual equipment, or remembered sacred procedures.
Period clothing and architecture need a narrower asset reference before production.
Modern festival presentation is not sufficient evidence for 1936.

## R6. Tày communities in the Cao Bằng uplands

### Source facts and geographic boundary

Bound this profile to Tày communities in Cao Bằng province as named in the 2019 heritage record, and keep it on the Vietnamese side of the border.
The government's heritage record identifies Then practice in this northern province [T1].
Holm's original fieldwork identifies Then practitioners among Tày communities and describes both male and female specialists [T2].
The UNESCO archive record supports community purposes such as peace, crops, and health, with musical accompaniment [T3].

The sources describe Then across several ethnic groups, but this proposed profile is specifically Tày.
Do not merge Tày, Nùng, Thái, or Zhuang communities into one regional religion.
Do not confuse the Thái ethnic designation in Vietnam with the state of Thailand.
There is also a source-level qualification about transmission.
The heritage summary emphasizes oral transmission, while Holm's research identifies textual repertoires.
Use neither as a universal assertion about every practitioner.

### Fictional gameplay direction

If France or another major directly controls the selected home area, the visit should address a specific local population and route system.
The controller may seek help for damaged supplies, food production, or a threatened approach without claiming that the community endorses its political authority.

Calm land aid should support crop recovery or local reconstruction consistent with the actual state and season.
Warrior guidance should concern nearby upland approaches, route preparation, supply storage, and defensive positioning.
Musical ritual is cultural context rather than a sonic weapon.
The religious imagery summarized in the sources must not become a recruitable supernatural army or an additional evolution.

### Visual and historical limits

Use a fictional community recovery scene with the practitioner among residents.
If an instrument is visible, its exact form requires a sourced local reference.
Do not copy ceremonial dress, texts, seals, or songs from modern recordings into an unverified 1930s scene.
The opened research abstract establishes the title and distinctions, but the full article was not accessible through the consulted route.
This is a defensible geographic and cultural profile with a remaining period-asset gate, not a completed reconstruction of historical ceremonial practice.

## Reserves and exclusions

The Alutiiq Museum provides unusually strong community evidence for Kodiak-area titles Kalla'alek and Samanaq, and explicitly describes practice continuing into the twentieth century [A1].
This is a defensible reserve if one of the six proposed profiles cannot pass the map or period check.
It should replace a blocked profile rather than automatically increase the launch roster.
A Kodiak profile would use the archipelago's own communities and local coastal aid, with no reuse of Yup'ik identity or sacred material.
Its exact game-map footprint remains unverified.

Sealaska Heritage Institute provides a strong Tlingit reserve with the title íx̱t' and documented concern for sacred objects and clan ownership [A2].
Its source describes historical community roles including military intelligence, but does not prove a specific active practitioner in 1936.
The profile would need a southeast Alaska home and its own period check.
Adding several Alaska cultures to one coarse game state would increase art and research costs without creating reliable regional play.
Keep this reserve outside the launch set unless it resolves a specific gap.

Do not force a Mongolian sacred-mountain variant solely because Mongolia is associated with the umbrella concept.
The primary heritage records consulted describe a mixture of traditions, interrupted continuity, and later revival around Burkhan Khaldun [M1, M2].
They do not identify a sufficiently precise game-period practitioner profile for this assignment.
The active sacred landscape is also a poor generic military construction site.

Sámi and northeast Indian possibilities are not rejected as cultures or historical practices.
They are not selected because this bounded pass did not obtain a sufficiently specific combination of local practitioner, period context, geographic home, and usable primary evidence.
Do not fill those gaps with a generic northern drum, pan-indigenous imagery, or an invented title.

## Bounded gameplay improvements

### One selected local purpose and one commitment

The visit should identify the named home area, its current local problem, and the two available aid purposes.
The government then commits to exactly one rite.
The alternative rite closes for that visit.
An accepted rite should require one concrete material commitment or operational sacrifice that fits its purpose.
The player should see the commitment, local scope, duration, and plausible downside before acceptance.

For land aid, prefer support equipment and a temporary construction commitment when the existing civilian crisis or recovery action can consume those resources meaningfully.
For warrior guidance, prefer supplied troops held in the home area and a supply package, with trucks used only where a real road-supported action makes sense.
A river or tundra community should not acquire a truck requirement merely to standardize a cost row.
The parent should settle exact amounts from major-country affordability and existing crisis costs.
Use no new spendable resource and no more than two ordinary spend types for this small event unless the final action has a concrete reason for a third.

The costs should buy the means to act on the rite, not purchase a guaranteed supernatural success.
Preparation can reduce foreseeable exposure or improve implementation of advice.
It must not reveal the hidden explanation of the visitor's ability.

### Real local need and meaningful outcomes

| Situation | Desired effect | Material risk or opportunity cost | Result that must remain possible |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Active civilian crisis in the home area | A substantial reduction of an owner-recorded crisis pressure or a meaningful recovery milestone | Relief supplies and local reconstruction capacity are committed | Partial relief, wasted supplies, or a concrete local setback |
| Calm home area | A substantial, temporary food or recovery improvement appropriate to that community | Labor or supplies are diverted from ordinary construction and military use | A failed season, wasted effort, or a limited result |
| Troops near the home area | A meaningful temporary improvement in local preparation, supply resilience, or defensive effectiveness | Troops and useful supplies remain committed locally | Bad route advice, lost equipment, exposed positions, or no useful advantage |
| Exceptional success | A striking local outcome that changes the current situation | The original commitment still matters | The observer still cannot establish the hidden cause with certainty |
| Backfire | A specific local harm with a finite cleanup path | Further resources may be needed for aftercare | The player can decline extra spending and live with the remaining consequence |

Do not resolve every success as a small national modifier.
Do not let the strongest result erase deaths, restore more damage than existed, or duplicate a recovery already awarded by another owner.
When a crisis has already ended, use its actual recovery state or retire that target.
The rite must not manufacture a new disaster merely to remain relevant.

### Memory and aftercare

Keep the persistent public information compact.
The player mainly needs the home area, selected aid purpose, active deadline, and whether the promised preparation was completed.
The event does not need separate faith, authenticity, favor, ritual power, fear, and prestige meters.

Remember whether the government welcomed, peacefully refused, or persecuted this visitor, whether the chosen commitment was honored, and which concrete local consequence occurred.
These are qualitative state and history facts rather than a new currency system.
Peaceful refusal ends the visit without a delayed curse, surprise penalty, or disguised continuation.
Persecution risks unrest only when there is evidence of local respect for this particular visitor.
Local support must not be guaranteed by cultural identity alone.

Offer at most one aftercare action for a harmful outcome.
It should repair a specific remaining burden, such as lost local stores, damaged preparation, or panic-driven disruption.
Charge for the resources actually used and never offer a repeatable purchase of favor.
The action should not reverse deaths, erase the historical fact of persecution, or create an unlimited Chaos reduction loop.
An ordinary rebuilding mission should have enough time for real action, normally at least 90 days under the current guidance.
A shorter deadline needs an actual emergency in the story and the relevant owner's timing contract.

### True Sight with usable uncertainty

True Sight is the only evolution proposed here.
It requires Chaos 400 or above and a recorded welcome.
The durable welcome can support one later forecast episode without reopening the consumed rite choice or maintaining an empty decision category for years.
Activation itself contributes zero Chaos.
The parent must settle the precise evolution pacing and whether any later loss of authority invalidates delivery.

Every forecast should identify one named state, one concrete danger family, and a bounded period in which preparation matters.
Examples of danger families are harmful weather affecting supplies, a natural disaster affecting buildings and civilians, or a military threat to a specific approach.
These are design directions, not authored prophecy text or a new threat-spawning menu.
The danger must be compatible with the target's actual geography and campaign conditions.

The player should be able to commit troops, supplies, or reconstruction capacity to a relevant preparation.
One forecast should present no more than two meaningful preparations and a decline path.
Where two preparations exist, their difference should be operational, such as protecting a threatened route or preserving supplies for recovery.
Do not create a row of small purchases that all improve the same hidden score.

| Forecast resolution | Interpretation the design must support | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Threat occurs and preparation helps | Advice was useful, with its source still uncertain | Lower eligible losses or a better local military outcome |
| Threat occurs and preparation is insufficient | Some dangers exceed the response or cannot be prevented | Reduced or unchanged harm within the threat owner's rules |
| A preventable threat is actually averted | Success of the response is distinct from a false alarm | Spend remains spent and the recorded prevention explains the outcome |
| No qualifying threat existed | The prediction was mistaken or deceptive | Wasted committed resources and possible bounded local panic |
| The wrong place or wrong danger was named | The forecast was concretely inaccurate | The wrong preparation yields little benefit while the real situation resolves normally |
| Control or authority is lost before execution | The original government can no longer fulfill this local action | Cancel obsolete future effects without granting benefits to the new controller |

The outcome record needs to distinguish a prevented event from a prediction that was never correct.
Otherwise rational preparation makes every successful warning look like fraud.
Do not generate an enemy attack merely to vindicate the prediction.
Do not treat troop placement as a means to prevent a natural earthquake or volcanic eruption.
Such preparation can protect supplies, support evacuation where an owner supports it, or improve recovery.
The event should retain an unavoidable-danger outcome where the warning is accurate but the available measures only limit harm.

### Event 013 ownership boundary

This review does not independently inspect or certify Event 013 code.
The parent has the actual disaster and relief overview and owns the source contract.
The design needs two explicitly different interfaces.

For an active disaster, Shaman selects a valid local incident and offers assistance through that incident's owner.
The owner remains responsible for severity, civilian losses, damage, relief completion, and cleanup.
Shaman must not decrement a second copy of the same pressure or add a duplicate relief reward.

For a future natural-danger forecast, the design needs an owner-authorized target and threat receipt, or another explicit forecasting contract that the actual owner supports.
If no such future-danger interface exists, it must be specified as parent-owned integration work.
Do not pretend that inspecting an already active crisis proves future prediction support.
Do not write a parallel disaster implementation inside Shaman to avoid the integration question.
Civilian panic or a failed preparation must enter the relevant shared consequence record only when the defined harm actually occurs.

### Delayed actions and AI

Before charging, starting, resolving, or extending any delayed action, recheck the current recipient's authority, the frozen home area, the chosen commitment, and the referenced threat or crisis.
Loss of control retires future Shaman effects and obsolete decisions.
It does not undo spent work as a free refund or erase the event's history.
Any refund of genuinely unspent resources requires one recorded settlement and belongs in the final lifecycle contract.

AI priorities should depend on actual local crisis severity, nearby military relevance, available supplies, and whether the promised preparation can be completed.
An AI at war with no troops or supply access near the home region should not select warrior aid simply because it has a high generic war weight.
A calm civilian recovery action can remain worthwhile if its local gain justifies the real commitment.
The AI must receive the same visible uncertainty and eligibility rules as the player.
It should not read a hidden fraud or supernatural result to avoid risk.
Exact weights and named campaign cases belong with `chaosx_ai_probability_auditor`.
No probability tool or engine verification was available or claimed in this review.

## Classification and stopping point

Minor Fire-Once is a reasonable proposal because the design promises one memorable local encounter and one associated evolution, with finite consequences.
Chaos level 1 is consistent with the baseline premise being available before the later True Sight threshold.
Cluster None is also reasonable if the parent confirms that no actual cluster contract applies.
These remain design recommendations until registry and namespace reconciliation is complete.

The plan has enough depth when it contains six verified region mappings, a single rite commitment, consequential local outcomes, one aftercare opportunity, and a usable True Sight forecast with proper owner integration.
The remaining effort should improve the exact state bindings, costs, timing, local presentation, AI cases, and cleanup.
Additional countries, religious institutions, focus trees, GUI windows, recruitable shamans, ritual crafting, global favor systems, extra evolution tiers, and extra art families would dilute the regional promise.
They are not recommended.

# Shaman near-completion improvement review

## Verdict and scope

Recommend retaining the completed design and stopping feature expansion.
The six specification parts contain enough depth for the requested regional encounter.
Three narrow clarifications below will strengthen goal fit and presentation without adding a mechanic, region, value, evolution, or asset family.
No blocking cultural substitution or need for additional cultural research was found in the reviewed design.

This is the second bounded review by the already instantiated `chaosx_improvement_loop_planner`.
It reviews design depth, cultural coherence, overbuilding, and the user's regional promise.
It does not audit arithmetic, payment transactions, probability calculations, or engine implementation.
Those subjects belong to the parent's other reviewers and implementation handoff.
Only this review document was written.
No specification or supplied source was edited.

The parent explicitly accepted the six cultural profiles, one rite aftercare opportunity, adapted nonmotor transport, one persistent cooperation value, one base rite, and up to three finite True Sight visions.
That acceptance supersedes the earlier proposal's narrower one-forecast suggestion.
All invented structural terms remain working labels, not final localisation.

## Reviewed material

All six authoritative specification parts were read in full, followed by the complete prior regional proposal.
The relevant supplied brief was checked again for the distinction between an actual local crisis and calm-state aid.

| Document | Reviewed design contribution |
| --- | --- |
| [Part 1: Core](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/e2429f23c85a/docs/specs/118_shaman_specs/118_shaman_spec_part_1_core.md) | Direct controller, selection, audience, cooperation, persecution, lifecycle, evolution entry |
| [Part 2: Rites](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/e2429f23c85a/docs/specs/118_shaman_specs/118_shaman_spec_part_2_rites.md) | One commitment, land needs, military locality, practical consequences, aftercare |
| [Part 3: True Sight](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/e2429f23c85a/docs/specs/118_shaman_specs/118_shaman_spec_part_3_true_sight.md) | Three-vision limit, source ownership, public information, preparation, adjudication |
| [Part 4: Regions](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/e2429f23c85a/docs/specs/118_shaman_specs/118_shaman_spec_part_4_regions.md) | Six communities, map and period limits, title and scene boundaries |
| [Part 5: Decisions, AI and Chaos](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/e2429f23c85a/docs/specs/118_shaman_specs/118_shaman_spec_part_5_decisions_ai_chaos.md) | Staged interaction budget, information parity, finite consequences and history |
| [Part 6: Presentation and achievements](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/e2429f23c85a/docs/specs/118_shaman_specs/118_shaman_spec_part_6_presentation_achievements.md) | Direction-only prose, four achievements, asset consumers and period-source gates |
| [Regional proposal](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/e2429f23c85a/docs/plans/118_shaman_plans/118_shaman_regional_design_review.md) | Original six-profile research, 21-entry source register, bounded improvement recommendations |
| [Supplied task state](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/e2429f23c85a/source_review/task_state.md) | Exact local aid and True Sight promise used for this review |

The review relies on the already opened primary evidence in the regional register.
No new web search was necessary because the final parts do not add an unsupported culture, practitioner title, sacred object, or historical personal identity.

## Disposition of the earlier proposal

| Earlier proposal | Disposition | Reason and accepted form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Six finite regional profiles | Accept as integrated | Part 4 retains the precise communities and research limits, including the Podkamennaya Tunguska correction and the narrow Tày identity |
| Equal underlying capability assumptions across cultures | Accept as integrated | Cultural identity never changes the hidden capability distribution, while actual conditions can change practical cooperation and delivery |
| Select the host before the regional profile | Accept as integrated | Profile count does not grant additional host tickets, preserving variety without a hidden national preference |
| Direct control and immutable cultural home | Accept as integrated | Subjects and allies do not pass control to an overlord, and a conqueror does not inherit or relabel the contact |
| One powerful rite chosen for a concrete local purpose | Accept with clarification M1 | Land needs are explicit and military work is bounded, but the calm-mode eligibility sentence should be more precise |
| A meaningful material commitment rather than small free bonuses | Accept as integrated | Preparation, supply, reconstruction and operational presence create a real choice, with substantial local results |
| Avoid inappropriate truck requirements | Accept the parent modification | Portable support substitutes where verified roads and infrastructure do not justify motor transport, without adding new stockpile types |
| Qualitative relationship memory without several meters | Modify and accept | One public Local Cooperation value is useful because it affects a small number of choices and has explicit causes, while hidden authenticity remains inaccessible |
| One bounded aftercare opportunity | Accept as integrated | The original rite has one finite follow-up, and later reconciliation is tied to an actual separate event-owned consequence rather than a permanent favor purchase |
| One later forecast episode | Modify and accept | Up to three visions better sustains the requested foresight relationship while preserving one active vision, a cooldown, consumed slots, finite closure and one evolution |
| Distinguish prevention, false alarm and unobservable outcomes | Accept as integrated | Part 3 separates observed facts from modelled reduction and avoids calling a preserved military frontier proof of supernatural prediction |
| Use the actual disaster and relief owners | Accept with clarification M2 | Active relief and future consequence prediction have separate contracts, with missing integrations identified rather than simulated by Shaman |
| Anonymous regional scenes with no recruitable portrait | Accept with adjustment M3 | Part 6 keeps grounded identity out of generated portrait consumers, while the shared True Sight scene needs a stronger local subject |
| Alutiiq and Tlingit as replacement reserves | Accept as integrated | They remain alternatives for a specific blocked profile and do not increase the launch quota |
| Additional countries, focus trees, custom windows, global favor or more evolutions | Reject expansion | None is needed to strengthen this regional promise and none should be introduced in the remaining handoffs |

## Material clarifications

### M1. Make calm-mode eligibility explicit for the selected state

**Importance: medium, design clarity.**

Part 1 deliberately allows the player to select a calm target while another state has a crisis.
That is a legitimate allocation choice within the reviewed regional selector.
The same part also describes scarce aid leaving a different crisis untreated.
The user's brief describes assistance to a selected state's actual civilian crisis, with harvest or recovery in calmer conditions.
Part 2 says the player selects an eligible need and that food mode also serves calm states, but does not state the selected-state calm predicate as directly as it states the other mode gates.

Clarify that calm seasonal food aid is valid only when the selected state has no actionable civilian crisis that the accepted land modes can address.
Where that state has several supported crises, the government chooses one actual need.
An active shortage can still use the food mode as crisis relief.
A calm state elsewhere in the region can remain selectable as an intentional allocation decision, with the unserved crisis visible in the target context.
This preserves the parent's target-choice depth without letting a calm-state label conceal an active problem in the very state receiving the rite.

This is a selector and explanatory-rule clarification.
It requires no new meter, automatic target switch, or forced choice of the single worst crisis in the whole region.
If the parent instead intends calm prosperity to remain selectable inside an actively afflicted state, record that as an explicit interpretation of the user's promise rather than leaving it implicit.

### M2. Preserve the distinct value of True Sight in full feature acceptance

**Importance: medium, acceptance clarity.**

Part 3 makes a sound distinction between Event 013's already public forecast and Shaman's hypothesis about a concrete consequence.
It also correctly refuses to infer secret enemy orders or score every held frontier as a proven prediction.
The military branch therefore remains a conditional warning and readiness opportunity based on observable vulnerability.
That is coherent as one part of the evolution.

Full feature acceptance should require at least one complete natural-consequence forecasting path through the real owner.
It must bind the named state, actual accepted job, consequence hypothesis, useful time window, preparation and an observable adjudication.
It must support a wrong or overstated component as well as a useful supported hypothesis.
The hypothesis or inquiry must provide concrete consequence information beyond simply repeating the existing official date and hazard family.
Its information can remain conditional and fallible.

A release with only the conditional military readiness branch, because every natural adapter remains unavailable, should be described as partial True Sight implementation.
It would provide useful local play but would weaken the requested development from ordinary guidance into specific foresight.
This clarification does not authorize new disaster generation, simulated enemy intent, guaranteed future casualty counts, or concealment of Event 013 information.
It makes the already required natural integration a meaningful completion condition.

### M3. Keep the shared True Sight image centered on local action

**Importance: low, presentation adjustment before the asset prompt is fixed.**

The Part 6 `RPT-VISION` row currently centers government staff checking a report and preparing supplies.
The regional scenes otherwise give the visitor and residents a clear practical role.
Using routine report checking as the shared image risks making the evolved relationship look like an administrative notification.
It also approaches the current writing and asset guidance's discouraged default of staff-table mystery.

Retain the existing single `RPT-VISION` consumer and its documentary treatment, but make an active local preparation the dominant subject.
The direction can show anonymous people strengthening shelter or moving supplies under a visible approaching danger, with the visitor present through posture and interaction rather than a centered face or invented costume.
Keep documents and official observation secondary if they remain in the composition.
Choose the particular setting only after the source and asset workers resolve the required period references.
Do not add a new portrait, sacred emblem, prophecy text, animated sequence, or six extra vision paintings.

## Cultural coherence assessment

Part 4 retains the difficult distinctions from the research instead of smoothing them into a generic regional shaman.
The Buryat title remains locally qualified.
The Evenki home stays in the basin supported by the principal study.
Jeju uses simbang and does not reenact the documented seasonal ceremony.
The Yup'ik profile preserves its southwest Alaskan boundary.
The Hmong profile retains the distinction between local community research and diaspora terminology evidence.
The Tày profile preserves the source qualification about oral and textual repertoires.
These are sufficient cultural design constraints for the present scope.

The constant hidden capability distribution and conditional controller examples preserve the same underlying uncertainty across cultures.
Local Cooperation is explicitly a relationship with the government, which prevents the value from becoming a judgment of a people's worth or credulity.
Occupation can affect access and reaction without determining truthfulness or supernatural potential.
Visible backing belongs to the fictional visitor's particular relationship rather than every member of the community.

The nonmotor transport adaptation resolves a concrete problem that a standard equipment quote would otherwise create for remote taiga, delta, and upland profiles.
The separate military gate is also appropriate for Jeju and any coarse map state.
Land aid remains a meaningful route where a genuinely local military effect cannot be supported.
No distant naval bonus, universal jungle ability, permanent ethnic unit bonus, or forced recruitment is substituted.

Period art and map bindings remain real implementation gates.
Their unresolved status does not justify expanding the roster or inventing historical evidence.
The accepted six-row target should remain visible in the completion record, with any disabled row or replacement explicitly accounted for.

## Depth and overbuilding assessment

The final design has a coherent sequence of decisions.
The government chooses how to receive the visitor, which local need deserves the single rite, whether to rush, how to handle the result, and how much preparation an uncertain later warning deserves.
Costs, local effects, authority loss, retained physical repairs, and persistent treatment memory give those choices consequences.
The four land modes serve different real needs within the same family and entitlement rather than adding four separate progression tracks.

One persistent cooperation value is proportionate to the relationship.
The staged native category and finite action pages avoid a large custom interface.
Up to three visions let the government reconsider its judgment over time, including after a poor first rite, while the cooldown and slot limit prevent a repeatable preparation service.
An active source disappearing consumes the issued slot rather than providing unlimited replacement searches.
No further vision tier or culture-specific ritual tree is needed.

The achievement set rewards sustained local recovery, actual frontier commitment, owner-recorded preparation, and different judgments across warnings.
The rare fourth achievement should remain explicitly opportunity-dependent.
Do not create extra disasters, force particular inquiry results, add more visions, or add automatic military false-alarm scoring merely to guarantee its availability.
Its rarity is a tuning matter for the designated reviewer, not a reason to expand the event.

The asset inventory is bounded by real consumers.
Six original regional scenes communicate six accepted homes, while category crops reuse their lineage.
The small shared icon families and four achievement subjects have distinct roles.
After M3, the remaining asset work should improve evidence and composition inside those rows rather than create more families.

## Stopping recommendation

Resolve M1 as a selected-state eligibility clarification, make M2 explicit in the implementation acceptance record, and adjust the existing M3 scene direction.
Then stop design expansion and complete the implementation handoff, evidence register, and downstream prompts already in progress.

Retain the accepted bounds of six regional profiles, one base rite, one public cooperation value, one rite aftercare opportunity, and one True Sight evolution with at most three visions.
Keep the researched reserve cultures as replacements only.
Do not add a country, faction, focus tree, custom window, recruitment surface, sacred-symbol collection, new spendable resource, extra evolution, or new generated portrait to fill a perceived quota.

The remaining uncertainties concern verification and execution of the accepted design.
Exact state footprints, period visual references, native modifier behavior, owner integration, arithmetic, payment safety, probability behavior, and live execution are not certified by this review.
The parent should record the disposition of M1 through M3 in the final integration record.
No additional improvement-loop pass is warranted unless a later implementation finding removes a core local effect or reveals a concrete contradiction in the accepted promise.

# Event 118 Shaman system architecture review

Date: 2026-10-23  
Role: chaosx_scripted_system_architect  
Disposition: planning only, for parent review  
Repository: klimPaskov/Chaos-Redux  
Pinned commit: 41bc4e5045a7b5c131be69dda2f08079d478634c

## 1. Decision and evidence boundary

Build Shaman as one actor and one fixed home-state contract with a small private lifecycle. Route food through the famine owner, disaster preparation and recovery through Event 013, and military guidance through one finite state modifier bound to the original country. A state is the minimum reliable native locality in the reviewed source. A cultural region can select that state, but it must not silently expand a one-state reward into a strategic-region or country reward.

The supplied-source gate is passed at team level. The parent reported 151 unique supplied sources reviewed. This review adds targeted repository evidence. It does not claim that every downloaded repository file was read in full. The evidence manifest records complete downloads separately from actual read ranges. No game execution, installed-documentation check, native modifier test, or HOI4 MCP test occurred. The environment is Linux scratch and the actual Windows checkout is unavailable.

The applicable role, current AGENTS.md, events, decisions and missions, subagents, ideas and modifiers, and map and state skills were read. The role's default patch permission is superseded by the parent planning-only assignment. No gameplay source was changed. The requested report and downloaded evidence are the only authored files in this subtask.

All names in sections marked **Proposed** are design contracts, not existing callable APIs. The observed API names below are exact source names.

## 2. Existing helper and owner map

| Observed symbol | Owner and scope | Inputs and observable outputs | Constraint for Shaman |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| call_natural_disaster | Shared public gateway, COUNTRY | Validated family, target, severity and policy inputs. Returns acceptance, rejection, sequence and resolved targets through its documented outputs. Accepted calls schedule physical disasters. | Never use it to observe a vision. Shaman must not call it merely to make a prediction true. |
| natural_disaster_enqueue_state_job | Private 013 owner, selected state and controller queue | Stores aligned job fields, reserves due date and schedules the hidden owner event. | Shaman does not append, remove, reorder or edit queue rows. |
| natural_disaster_prepare_job_outcome_snapshot | Private 013 owner | Copies current deaths, damage, phase, warning, chain and physical-origin state into job inputs. | This is not a future-consequence simulation. It cannot supply an exact prophecy of future losses. |
| natural_disaster_apply_warning_direction | Private 013 owner, STATE | Persists one selected warning protection, adds preparation score and starts its lock. | Do not call it as an extra fourth warning action or add preparation score directly. |
| natural_disaster_offer_neighbor_relief_for_gods_of_africa | Explicit 012-to-013 bridge, donor COUNTRY | Requires the regular gods_of_africa_protected_participant target, exact route and donor gates. Selects a live recovery card before owner payment, then opens inbound relief and writes bridge receipts. | This is a named 012 bridge, not a generic free relief API. It is precedent for a dedicated 118 adapter. |
| natural_disaster_execute_reassessment | Private 013 owner, STATE | Reads the current phase work score, determines full, partial or failed work, advances phases or closes the card. | Shaman may contribute bounded work through a new adapter. It does not force phase completion or close a card. |
| famine_refresh_reserve_capacity | Famine owner, STATE | Computes daily need, logistics, capacity and target. First initialization can seed baseline reserves. | A paid Shaman grant must measure its own added stock after any owner initialization. The baseline seed is not Shaman relief. |
| famine_add_reserves | Famine owner, STATE | Consumes import amount and request, source and actor proof fields. Clamps to headroom, returns actual added stock, remaining stock, capacity and result. | Suitable inner mutation for a new validated harvest adapter. Its positive proof fields alone are insufficient cross-system identity proof. |
| famine_consume_reserve_for_relief | Famine owner, STATE | Debits exact accepted reserve units and produces bounded temporary rationing relief. Returns actual consumed stock and granted relief. | It is not a generic removal helper and should not be used to create a rite backfire. |
| famine_mark_relief_access | Famine owner, STATE | Marks verified relief access and clears the no-humanitarian-corridor proof. | Food creation alone does not prove a transport corridor. Do not call this for an ordinary blessing. |
| apply_shared_hygiene_measures and related apply/revoke effects | Biological shared owner, COUNTRY | Adds or removes country flags and ideas read by outbreak systems. | They are broad country policies, not a local disease cure. |
| black_plague_finish_shared_state_action | Black Plague private owner, STATE with matching action ownership | Reads an existing owner action and applies treatment, sanitation, quarantine or other family-specific consequences. | Do not call without the owner action lifecycle or fabricate its active flags. |
| add_human_state_dynamic_modifier | Shared helper, STATE | Installs the requested state modifier for every existing human country and records duration. | Wrong beneficiary contract for a boon restricted to one Shaman host. |
| gods_of_africa_select_industry_site and related industry owner effects | Event 012 industry owner, HOST or ACTOR as documented | Select, bind, fund, review and retire a finite repair service on one frozen site. | Useful identity, payment and cleanup precedent. Do not call or copy the 012 contract into 118. |

Sources: [013 runtime and public ownership contract, lines 11–61][S1], [013 job representation, lines 1750–2065][S2], [warning and relief owner effects, lines 6368–6448 and 6940–7117][S3], [famine owner API notes][S4], [reserve mutation, lines 2430–2762][S5], [shared biological measures][S6], [Black Plague actions, lines 125–226][S7], [shared modifier helper, lines 925–1130][S8], and [012 industry contract][S9].

## 3. Truly local warrior guidance

### 3.1 Recommended representation

Use one proposed shaman_local_guidance dynamic modifier held by the frozen home STATE and bound to the exact original actor COUNTRY. Store strength and original expiry on the Shaman record. The modifier reads those values through deliberately documented scope paths.

The enable condition must prove the state, actor, generation, authority and original controller binding. ## 4. Event 013 integration

### 4.1 Existing forecasts already reveal the scheduled disaster

An accepted 013 call makes the disaster family, state, severity, hazard class and scheduled date available immediately. Acknowledgment changes only the alert. Therefore True Sight cannot present those queue facts as uniquely revealed knowledge. It may refer to the official forecast, then make a separate uncertain claim about a concrete consequence.

013 currently owns actual civilian deaths, building damage, disruption, physical continuation, work phases, foreign relief and recovery. Its control-transfer path moves complete delayed-job rows without changing reserved due dates and preserves source and report responsibilities. The Shaman extension must preserve those properties. [013 overview, lines 11–61 and 121–174][S1]

A useful natural vision names one existing state and accepted sequence, one predicted component, an explicit threshold within that component, and a horizon. For example, the proposal can select transport damage above an owner-defined threshold, given present transport exposure. It must not compare casualty counts directly against building levels to manufacture a supposedly objective dominant component.

The prediction is a cached hypothesis. It may use current exposure and an uncertain Shaman interpretation. It must not consume future RNG, run hidden outcomes early, query a future AI plan, or force a follow-up. A follow-up can be named only if 013 already owns an accepted queued job with a valid physical cause. A family merely capable of producing a chain is insufficient proof that the chain is pending.

### 4.3 Component mitigation and honest outcome evidence

The existing preparation score activates broad death and building mitigation. Increasing it from 1 to 2 does not define an additional proportional benefit. Setting it from 0 to 1 grants broad effects and collides with the three existing warning choices. Consequently Shaman needs a separate single-component credit and must not mutate the warning choice, protection, score or lock.

A reasonable initial proposal is to multiply the matching component by 0.80 for normal preparation or 0.65 for exceptional preparation. Cap the total extra reduction supplied by external credits at 35% of the component remaining after existing owner mitigation. Only one Shaman credit can be consumed for the same receipt. Existing warning, resilience, caps and chain behavior remain authoritative.

For transport preparation, apply the factor only inside 013's eligible transport-building damage path. For casualty preparation, apply it only in the casualty request before the Deaths owner mutates population. Do not multiply the whole family building scale and call that transport-specific protection.

013's current building helper measures native damage before and after a command and records the actual positive delta. Its casualty helper records the actual Deaths-system return. These are appropriate final consequence facts. [Damage and death application, lines 4980–5160 and 5425–5532][S14]

A proposed extension may also record the owner's resolved pre-credit component request and post-credit request. The difference is a modelled reduction in requested damage. It is not observed proof of buildings or lives saved, because native caps, eligibility and engine application can change the actual result. Do not execute a second unmitigated command to measure a counterfactual.

Recommended outcome distinctions are:

- The observed component crossed the predicted threshold.
- The owner's resolved threat request crossed the threshold and preparation reduced the request before its measured application.
- The predicted component did not reach its threshold.
- The matching job did not execute within the horizon, so readiness was unused.
- The source or state became ineligible, so the receipt was cancelled.

Only the first two provide relevant evidence for the vision, with the second explicitly grounded in the owner's modelled threat. An absence of disaster is not proof that supernatural guidance prevented one.

These are 013 work units, not food, population recovery, building levels or an instant cure.

The observed rescue, stabilization and reconstruction success thresholds are 3, 4 and 5. Normal rescue and stabilization actions contribute 1, while reconstruction actions contribute 2. The proposed blessing can materially improve a response without owning the whole crisis. Negative recovery burden and partial work remain in the owner score. The adapter returns the amount actually accepted. [013 action scores][S15] [013 reassessment, lines 10400–10578][S16]

Do not set search, water, chain-prevention or reconstruction action flags unless that named physical action occurred. Do not clear aftermath modifiers directly. Do not create extra mission capacity or reopen a closed card. Event 013 alone decides whether the accumulated contribution advances the response.

## 5. Famine relief and calm harvest

### 5.1 Existing reserve units and actual effect

The famine owner stores food in thousand-person-days. Its daily need is based on state population in thousands. A covered-day grant is therefore:

**budget = frozen daily need × covered days**

The parent direction of 21 normal or 35 exceptional covered days is coherent with the existing ledger. The owner must clamp actual deposits to reserve headroom and return the actual credited amount. Freeze daily need at commitment so population or scope changes cannot enlarge an already purchased entitlement.

Stock contributes 1.5 relief points per covered day, up to a relief cap of 35. The food-score formula weights relief by 1.2 and divides the total by 2.5. Thus 21 fully stored days can reduce that score by at most 15.12 through this component, and the relief cap limits this component to 16.8. Stock can also remove the additional exhaustion penalty. Stage recovery still requires the owner's below-threshold recovery windows. A blessing does not instantly reset famine stage or restore dead population. [Famine system][S17] [Famine core effects and constants][S4]

Capacity is not a universal 45 days. The current owner computes capacity from daily need, 45 base days and a logistics factor clamped between 0.25 and 1.25. Severe transport damage can therefore leave too little headroom for the full award. The receipt must expose actual units accepted and any retained credit rather than imply that the entire headline duration was immediately deposited. [Capacity and reserve mutation, lines 2430–2762][S5]

Country existence and state validity are different checks. Do not use a country exists predicate as proof of a saved state reference. A regular event target is appropriate for the originating synchronous call chain, but must not be the only persistent identity for delayed work.

Keep public values to one or two meaningful player-facing quantities if the parent needs them. Lifecycle stage, receipt, generation, authority epoch, retry and source-job fields stay hidden. A status or predicted date is not an excuse to add another spendable currency.

### 9.2 Four cost families and real commitment

The parent-selected spendable families are PP, support equipment, trucks and civilian production commitment. Each displayed choice uses at most three inline resources. Military presence is a gate or commitment and does not create a fifth manpower charge.

A factory availability floor is not a debit. The reviewed 013 missions make a real timed production commitment through consumer_goods_factor at 0.05, or 0.10 for heavy work. The warning factory floor is eligibility. The pinned modifier list contains civilian_factory_use, but no fixed-count reservation has been proven here. [013 mission burden, lines 5122–5175][S20] [Modifier list, lines 346–347][S11]

Prefer an explicit timed percentage production commitment with a named start and end, or separately validate fixed-count civilian_factory_use before specifying exact reserved factories. Do not advertise two factories for 30 days if the actual implementation merely checks that two are available.

Quote, affordability gate, debit and display must use the same cached values. Stock checks accept exactly the quoted amount and reject anything below it. Sale integration, if used by the parent, must preserve the quote version through the click or explicitly refresh the offer before commitment. It must not quote one amount and debit another.

Before payment, validate owner readiness and exact target. After a measured debit, either commit the matching owner receipt in the same effect chain or mark the transaction unresolved and reverse only the current owned stock debit once. Never refund an earlier successful attempt. A finite production reservation is released through its own exact receipt. Already elapsed production time is not refundable stock.

Failure, refusal after commitment, uncertainty or an unused prediction does not itself authorize a refund. Refund is for a failed or cancelled transaction boundary as explicitly designed, not for an unfavorable rite outcome.

### 9.3 Terminal behavior matrix

| Boundary | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Duplicate click or delayed callback | Return or display the existing receipt. No new spend, outcome draw, credit, duration or base rite. |
| Stale popup | Revalidate frozen actor, state, authority, quote and owner target. Reject before payment and refresh the offer if still meaningful. |
| Owner rejects before payment | Charge nothing and keep a concrete unavailable reason. |
| Owner accepts less relief | Record actual accepted work or food. Preserve only a documented finite remainder, never silently credit the full nominal award. |
| Direct control lost | Retire the old military binding and cancel unused 118 authority. Preserve 013 job due dates and source receipts. Already delivered food and physical 013 consequences remain owner facts. |
| Actor annexed or generation replaced | Cleanup through original stored identities. Do not attach service or refund to a replacement incarnation. |
| Country ROOT changes in callback | Resolve the saved original actor and state. Never reinterpret the new callback ROOT as the payer or beneficiary. |
| Native modifier missing unexpectedly | Do not reinstall a fresh full duration. Record unresolved service and reconcile against original expiry. |
| Modifier removal fails or cannot be proved | Preserve the old identity and unresolved evidence. Do not clear pointers first and lose the ability to remove the exact binding. |
| Owner phase or job changed | Ask owner to reject, expire or match its receipt. Do not migrate the credit to an unrelated new crisis. |
| Time horizon ends without a matching threat | Close as unused readiness. Costs and completed preparations remain factual. |
| Home state later regains control | No new grant. Any permitted resumption uses only the original unexpired record and no fresh payment. |
| Persecution, peaceful refusal or base rite complete | Parent outcome closes or makes contact dormant. Cleanup must not leave a selectable second base rite. |

Control-change work should be routed through the existing narrow callback or a bounded registered-state owner. In the documented on_state_control_changed context, ROOT is the new controller, FROM the old controller and FROM.FROM the state. Any implementation must preserve that scope contract.
