# Shaman decision and mission review

## Working review status

This is a source-only planning audit for requested Event 118, original catalog identity 129.
All action names, review identifiers and suggested labels are working design labels, not final localisation.
Final disposition: all five pending planning-contract groups are resolved in the frozen Parts 1, 2, 3 and 5 after the parent applied the accepted corrections.
The final affected-source clarification also resolves the zero-reserve adverse-food ambiguity and confirms that Part 3's trailing-comma edit is punctuation only.
This closes the bounded decision and mission planning audit, with the native implementation checks listed below retained as limitations.
No gameplay, localisation, asset, catalog or external application was edited by this auditor.

The parent corrected several significant issues during the audit.
The reviewed changes distinguish hostile frontier loss from void transfers, give military readiness its own absolute expiry, make persecution reconciliation a 30-day work period rather than an expired entry prerequisite, and distinguish a stored draw from the effect that can actually be delivered after a crisis ends.
A second bounded correction check resolved the equipment escrow and upgrade-work risks, the inquiry PP rule and the panic-offer timing conflict.
The final diff-only pass verified one deferred-credit settlement, fixed medical expiry, exact state allocations and focus-loss handling, original-payer forfeiture, reconciliation payment closure, source-change precedence and final follow-up preservation.

The review covers Parts 1, 2, 3 and 5 and the relevant sections of the system architecture review.
The parent was still preparing the other parts.
Their future implementation contracts are not treated as already reviewed here.
The parent reported that all 151 supplied project sources passed the team source gate before design.
This subtask independently read the supplied decision-auditor role, current AGENTS.md, relevant Events, Decisions and Missions, Subagents, Ideas and Modifiers and AI Strategies guidance, payment and validation references, and the GUI skill's interaction-budget section.
It did not duplicate the team's entire supplied-source review.

## Finding history and final dispositions

The explanatory paragraphs preserve the failure cases and recommended contracts from the earlier review.
The current disposition at each finding and the final closure table govern the present conclusion.
Earlier proposed alternatives are not additional requirements once the parent has selected a precise rule.

### H01. Make escrow and upgrade work credit exact

**Current disposition: resolved at design level.**
The parent resolved escrow, actual credited work, pending full strength and military partial-refund timing in the second reviewed correction.
Final Part 2 line 32 separately divides measured dispatched and held balances across the frozen selected states, assigns integer remainders by ascending state ID and refunds only the stored held allocation.
The paragraphs below preserve the original failure case and the exact contract used for the correction.

**Affected surfaces:** Part 2, material commitment and partial state loss. Part 3, preparation choices and military readiness. Part 5, D04, D08, D09 and M02.

The original draft did not distinguish the already consumed limited payment, the upgrade delta and refundable held material.
The parent added an immutable limited/full quote pair, a single delta debit, rollback of only the new delta, and rejection after a limited credit is consumed.
Those changes address the main duplicate-payment risk.

Two details required correction after the first parent edit and were corrected in the second changed-section review.
First, the added rule completes full work at original start plus 14 days and permits a one-day minimum after a later upgrade.
That counts idle days after a finished seven-day limited project as useful work.
For example, limited work completes on day 7, an upgrade occurs on day 20, and that superseded rule delivered full preparation on day 21.
Only seven days of limited work and one new day were performed.
Credit actual recorded work days, capped by the completed limited requirement.
Set the upgrade due date to upgrade time plus the remaining full work requirement.
An upgrade on day 3 therefore finishes on day 14, while an upgrade on day 20 after seven completed days requires seven more days.
Use the same calculation with three and seven days for an imminent follow-up.
The one-day-before-impact gate still applies.

Second, replacing the limited owner credit with full strength at upgrade acceptance could activate the stronger protection before the extra work completes.
Stage the replacement as pending and publish full usable strength only when paid work and any military presence requirement both succeed.
An existing completed limited credit may remain usable while the upgrade is pending, with one logical response identity and no second consumption.
If the source consumes that limited credit first, the pending upgrade cannot create another protection credit.
Its terminal result must settle only its own undelivered balance.

Define equipment escrow explicitly.
The full quoted equipment amount is removed from usable stock once at commitment.
The receipt divides that measured debit into dispatched and held amounts.
Held means refundable event-owned escrow, not equipment left usable in the national stockpile.
For each resource and transaction, total paid equals consumed plus currently held plus returned.
No path can both consume and refund the same held unit.
Full military work completion ends its production burden but must preserve held equipment until the combined work-and-presence resolver succeeds or awards the partial package.

For a multi-state rite, partition each resource's held amount across the immutable selected states at payment.
Use a deterministic remainder rule so the partitions sum exactly to the actual held total.
Do not recompute a new fraction after each loss.
For 75 trucks, dispatch is 38 and held is 37.
Three state allocations could be 13, 12 and 12 in frozen state order.
Repeated state loss then returns at most 37 trucks, even if callbacks arrive separately or repeat.

### H02. Publish cooperation and award classification once for deferred delivery

**Current disposition: resolved at design level.**
Final Part 2 line 173 gives each rite one cooperation-settlement receipt, keeps deferred credit pending, settles on first useful delivery using the applicable delivered class, and settles neutrally if the credit expires unused.
Final Part 2 line 98 allows a qualifying medical recurrence to consume only the remaining original 30-day window.
It cannot begin a fresh mitigation duration.
The explicit inconclusive class for a reduced three-day food conversion remains distinct from the stored hidden draw.

**Affected surfaces:** Part 1, cooperation changes. Part 2, disease conversion and converted or undeliverable outcomes. Part 5, the exceptional manifestation award.

The parent resolved the original ambiguity that could turn an adverse medical draw into positive readiness or apply a repair penalty to an already repaired site.
The added classification rule is a substantial improvement.
The earlier text classified unused medical readiness as inconclusive unless later delivery proved the promised effect.
Without an explicit publication boundary, completion could subtract 5 cooperation, later delivery could add the original positive award, and expiry or duplicate delivery could classify it again.

Keep the original draw, observable delivery and published cooperation settlement as separate fields.
Recommended boundary: deferred readiness is pending at rite completion and changes neither cooperation nor Chaos then.
On the first positive qualifying owner delivery, settle its delivered outcome once.
If it expires entirely unused, settle inconclusive once if that is the intended penalty.
Cancellation or an unusable result remains neutral under the parent's new rule.
Later food installments, recurring callbacks and report reopening cannot change the settled classification or repeat the award.
If the parent prefers immediate inconclusive settlement, it must explicitly forbid a later second cooperation change and describe later delivery as history only.

The earlier medical conversion also needed an exact recurrence consumption contract.
State which owner-family recurrence qualifies, require it to be a new valid outbreak within the saved 30-day window, consume the readiness once, and give the resulting mitigation an absolute expiry that cannot be renewed by subsequent outbreaks.
Preserving the original percentage alone does not define whether protection lasts 14, 45 or 60 days after consumption, or only until readiness expiry.
The parent should choose one of those existing duration meanings explicitly.
No recurrence is created to make the credit usable.

### M01. Complete the PP and reconciliation payment lifecycle

**Current disposition: resolved at design level.**
Inquiry PP and panic-offer persistence were resolved in the second reviewed correction.
Final Part 3 line 168 consumes reconciliation PP and equipment at valid commitment, denies refunds after later cancellation or authority loss, returns only the measured debit on a same-transaction start failure, and charges nothing for stale confirmation.

**Affected surfaces:** Part 1, persecution reconciliation. Part 3, inquiry and false-alarm reconciliation. Part 5, D07 and D11.

The initial inquiry charged 40 political power without a stated cancellation, authority-loss or source-invalidation refund rule.
The half-held equipment rule cannot answer a PP refund question.
Recommended contract: charge the quoted PP once at valid inquiry commitment, retain it once the inquiry has begun, cancel without a result on lost authority or invalid source, and reject a stale request before payment.
Write equivalent explicit rules for D11 rather than depending on an informal resemblance to aftercare.
If a payment fails before acceptance, return only this action's measured debit and publish no successful work receipt.

Panic lasts 14 days and reconciliation also takes 14 days.
Even an immediate start normally leaves no positive remaining panic to remove at completion.
D11's requirement for actual remaining panic also shortens the advertised 30-day offer.
The narrowest clarification preserves a single 30-day offer keyed to the original qualifying panic receipt, permits cooperation repair after natural panic expiry, and gives no negative Chaos award when no remaining burden was actually removed.
The tooltip must not promise early removal that its timing cannot deliver.
Alternatively, choose an explicit earlier burden-removal boundary and retain a separate 14-day cooperation-work result.

Persecution's original impossible timing is resolved in the rechecked text.
Its offer opens immediately for 30 days, and its 30 quiet days are work checked at completion.
The original 90-day disruption can therefore still have remaining duration when work finishes.

### M02. State source-change and cutoff precedence

**Current disposition: resolved at design level.**
Final Part 3 lines 162 through 172 preserve the physical owner outcome first, require explicit same-job proof for compatible revisions, apply the actual execution cutoff to advanced dates and settle unready paid work without retrospective protection.
The danger-window end plus seven days is the finite missing-receipt cutoff.
Late receipts may correct factual history but cannot reopen payment, response entitlement, achievement or Chaos awards.

**Affected surfaces:** Part 3, candidate identities, preparation, owner credits and hard cases. Part 5, confirmation and payment rules.

The draft correctly binds natural protection to sequence, job, state, component and revision and forbids moving it to another disaster.
It must also say what happens when an owner changes a planned date without replacing the physical job, revises a component, reports an outcome before a late callback, or returns no receipt at the end of the observation window.

Before payment, a changed quote or incompatible source snapshot invalidates the visible confirmation and requires a refreshed offer.
Never silently charge a fresh quote that the player did not approve.
For an already paid action, preserve its actual quote and original expiry.
An owner-approved compatible revision may retain the same physical identity, but cannot extend the original benefit window or infer additional completed work.
An advanced execution date that makes the promised work impossible must route to the existing cancellation or partial-result policy with its actual held balance.
An incompatible revision is void and cannot retarget.
At the final observation cutoff, an unavailable authoritative receipt resolves as unobservable, rather than retaining an active vision forever or fabricating a false alarm.
Once adjudicated, a later callback returns the stored result.

Use the frozen meaningful threshold when judging a natural hypothesis.
The pre-Shaman qualifying request governs whether a threat existed.
The post-Shaman reduced request must never make successful protection look like a false warning.
The owner's exact prevention receipt has precedence over the generic disproved branch.

### M03. Make the single follow-up window and final closure compatible

**Current disposition: resolved at design level.**
The parent added phase serialization that prevents vision issue during rite selection, work or aftercare and restricts overlap to inquiry plus its own preparation.
Final Part 3 line 23 retains an earned third-vision follow-up through its original window and permits paid follow-up work to finish before natural retirement.
Final Part 3 line 160 withdraws issued unpaid offers when evolution is disabled, permits paid inquiry to finish without opening new preparation, preserves already paid preparation and forbids new upgrades while disabled.

**Affected surfaces:** Part 1, ending the relationship. Part 2, aftercare. Part 3, third vision and reconciliation. Part 5, phase table.

The phase budgets are sound if the scheduler treats them as mutually exclusive gameplay states.
Write the invariant that only one optional follow-up offer or follow-up work item can be active for the encounter.
Its 30-day acceptance deadline is stored once at its qualifying result and does not refresh when a report is opened, an adverse guidance modifier is abandoned, or an offer is shown again.
A follow-up committed before that deadline may finish afterward.

The third vision closes future visions, but its earned reconciliation offer and any paid follow-up must retain their original window and expiry until settled.
Use closing rather than fully deleted for that final phase.
Separate end-contact closure from destruction of durable history, refund proof and pending owner settlements.
A high-Chaos welcome must not issue the first vision during rite selection, an active rite or its live aftercare window.
One phase lock should enforce the existing action budget, without creating another player-facing meter.

The evolution-off rule also needs a terminal rule for an already issued but unpaid vision and an inquiry in progress.
The existing paid-response protection is appropriate.
Unpaid opportunities should close or observe to their original cutoff according to one explicit rule, without a new issue slot, new draw or renewed offer when the setting returns.

### M04. Keep lost-actor refunds and target authority exact

**Current disposition: resolved at design level.**
Final Part 1 line 118 and Part 2 line 32 cancel the whole guidance package on focus loss while isolating a supporting-state loss to that state.
Final Part 2 line 34 forfeits held equipment if the original paying country has ceased to exist and forbids inheritance by a conqueror, release or reused tag.
Exact incarnation and binding proof remains an implementation obligation of the already specified receipt contract.

**Affected surfaces:** Parts 1 and 2, authority loss. Part 5, immutable confirmation and cleanup.

The rechecked hostile-control rule now records the military threatened outcome before authority cleanup and treats non-hostile transfer as void.
That fixes the principal contradiction.
Retain the original country incarnation and state authority epoch in every payment and owner binding, not only the country tag and action generation.
An annexed payer cannot receive a refund through a successor, conqueror or later incarnation of the same tag.
Choose an explicit terminal policy for held equipment when the original payer no longer exists, such as recorded unrecoverable escrow.
Do not create or restore a country to deliver a refund.

For partial military state loss, preserve the original state set and paid allocation.
State explicitly whether loss of the selected operational focus cancels the entire pending package or permits the remaining frozen states to complete.
Neither path may silently select a new focus or rerun the rite outcome.
Any surviving benefit must satisfy the original-actor binding and the specified finish requirements.

Keep popup tombstones until the exact old popup's closure path has retired its snapshot.
An old cancel option may close that popup but may not clear a newer action, response lock or receipt.

The inspected draft gives three, two or one work units for exceptional, effective or inconclusive results and clamps to the meaningful shortfall.
It explicitly avoids awarding unperformed search, evacuation or prevention flags.
That is a suitable owner boundary for planning.
Its no-longer-needed conversion and aftercare still inherit the settlement rules above.

## Cost and production audit

The draft stays within four spendable types across the whole event family and at most three on any listed paid action.
The production commitment is consumer-goods factor for a finite duration.
It is not a reserved count of civilian factories or percentage points of all factories.
The local Event 013 source uses consumer_goods_factor in its timed mission modifier, and the reviewed modifier reference separately lists civilian_factory_use as a flat reservation field.
No fixed-count factory reservation was demonstrated in this audit.

| Action | Motor-mode spendable types | Carried-supply mode | Required settlement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Initial rite | Support equipment, trucks, production factor: 3 | Support equipment, production factor: 2 | Full measured debit, dispatched/held split, one completion or cancellation |
| Limited or full response | Support equipment, trucks, production factor: 3 | Support equipment, production factor: 2 | Same split, exact source-bound readiness |
| Limited-to-full upgrade | Equipment delta and replacement production factor: at most 3 | Support delta and replacement factor: 2 | Never a second whole payment or retroactive industry charge |
| Inquiry | Political power: 1 | Same | PP consumed at valid start, exact transaction-failure refund only |
| Rite aftercare | Political power and support equipment: 2 | Same | Spent at commitment, one finite work result |
| Persecution or panic reconciliation | Political power and support equipment: 2 | Same | PP and equipment consumed at valid start, exact transaction-failure refund only |
| Selection, review, dismissal and ordinary end contact | 0 | Same | Cannot reroll, restart an offer or create a new payment |

Troop presence is a non-consumed operational requirement.
It does not deduct manpower, immobilize divisions or silently add a fifth resource.
Transport substitution correctly removes each truck cost and adds two support-equipment units, without creating an unreviewed local transport stockpile.

The current phrase production-commitment gate needs a precise implementation predicate.
An eligibility floor must remain separate from the factor that is actually applied.
Do not imply that passing a factory-count threshold reserves that number of factories.
The display must show the authoritative factor and duration, with any estimated industrial impact clearly identified as an estimate.

The supplied guidance requires matching resource texticons, inclusive affordability at the exact quote, and one authoritative quote feeding display, available, custom-cost state and debit.
The four audited drafts promise this but contain no final native sprite identifiers or completed cost localisation.
That is appropriate for working labels, but icon-token verification and base, blocked and tooltip key coverage remain implementation work.
No visual fit or native cost-row rendering is claimed.

## Category, mission and AI notes

The largest phase has three target rows plus browse and return, for five visible rows.
Ordinary gameplay phases have two to four actions.
The planned maximum is two simultaneous missions, with M03 represented inside M02 rather than a third independent timer.
Local Cooperation is the only persistent public mechanic value.
Its range, strained/workable/strong bands, current cause and practical effects are stated.
Dates, targets and observed deliveries are ordinary facts and do not require separate persistent meters.

| Work item | Owner and region | Duration and objective | Result and duplicate risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M01 rite | Original host, one state or frozen local military set | 21 normal or 7 urgent days after one paid commitment | Frozen outcome or explicit conversion, entitlement never returns |
| Inquiry | Same active vision and source | 5 days, or 3 for imminent follow-up | One public-evidence result, no new identity draw |
| M02 natural preparation | Original host, exact accepted job and component | 7/14 normal or 3/7 emergency days, finish one full day before execution | One limited or full credit, no source duplication |
| M02/M03 military preparation | One original frontier state | Paid work plus seven observed consecutive presence days for full | Full, partial or unused readiness, original expiry retained |
| Rite aftercare | Same result, state and owner | One 30-day offer and 14-day work period | One cooperation settlement and one mode-specific contribution |
| Persecution reconciliation | Home state and original reaction | One 30-day offer and 30 quiet work days | Shortens only the remaining owned disruption |
| Panic reconciliation | Exact false-alarm reaction | One 30-day offer and 14-day work period | Original receipt retains eligibility after panic expires, cooperation repairs once |

The short timers are justified by a visiting practitioner or an accepted imminent threat, with separate 90-day rite selection.
At the earliest normal natural issue date, 21 days remain.
Five inquiry days plus 14 full-work days plus one safety day use 20 days and are feasible.
At the earliest emergency date, 8 days remain.
Seven full-work days plus the safety day are feasible, while a three-day inquiry followed by full work is not.
The AI inquiry gate correctly conditions spending on leaving useful response time.
The human tooltip should describe the remaining limited choice when inquiry makes full preparation too late.

AI eligibility must run before weighting and again before payment.
The draft appropriately forbids hidden identity, stored outcome and support-draw inputs and preserves harmless refusal or dismissal fallbacks.
The separate probability auditor owns numerical pools and Chaos reachability.
For full military preparation, use verified present forces or an explicitly supported feasibility predicate.
Do not assume that ordinary AI will move divisions in time, and do not issue battle plans or manufacture enemy attacks to make the objective succeed.
No warning may create a disaster or replace unavailable owner evidence with a guessed outcome.

## Meaningful source scenarios

These are contract calculations and branch reviews, not executed gameplay tests.

| Scenario | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Stock exactly equals the frozen quote | Selection, blocked display and debit agree, with no strict-greater-than rejection |
| Price changes while a confirmation is open | Reject or visibly refresh before payment, never charge an unseen current price |
| Three-state rite loses states in different orders | Only each state's stored held allocation returns, total refund never exceeds original held equipment |
| Full military quote 100 support and 25 trucks, limited quote 50 and 10, presence fails | Return 50 support and 12 trucks from held escrow, leaving 50 support and 13 trucks spent |
| Completed limited response upgrades much later | Credit actual completed work, never idle calendar days, and preserve the original readiness expiry |
| Upgrade transaction fails | Restore the prior limited state and refund only the new measured delta once |
| Enemy captures the predicted state on the completion boundary | Store the observed threat first, cancel authority-bound benefits second, prevent both a successful hold and a void overwrite |
| Outbreak ends before completion and never recurs | No new illness, no fabricated benefit, one explicit terminal cooperation classification |
| Unrelated disaster strikes the same state | It cannot consume or validate the old job-specific credit |
| Third vision creates a valid follow-up | Close new opportunities while retaining that single earned window and paid settlement |
| Old callback runs after closure or generation replacement | No new payment, refund, benefit, cooperation change, Chaos award or mutation of the newer record |

## Source support, backing and observable evidence

### Natural hypotheses

P10's 57 and 60 percent calculations are correct for the original 20/50/30 identity prior.

They do not describe consequence occurrence, correct prophecy, prevented harm, useful preparation or achievement success.

The shared hidden identity persists across the encounter.
Later warnings therefore must not be represented as three unrelated draws from a fresh 57 or 60 percent population.
Conditioning on observed outcomes, retained contact or earlier evolution can also alter the identity mixture of the surviving population.
The proposals do not define a full joint probability model for warning components, changing campaign state and delivered outcomes.
No binomial success rate, campaign accuracy estimate or expected number of correct prophecies is justified.

Supported hypotheses can fail to reach their consequence thresholds.
Unsupported hypotheses can match an outcome by coincidence.
The adjudicator must inspect the exact owner receipt and the named component, never the hidden source-support bit.
Military warnings depend on visible vulnerability and later state-control evidence, so P10's support probabilities do not apply to military accuracy.

The AI information rule is correctly stated in S5.
Current geography, public forecast, actual crisis, observed inquiry findings, time remaining and affordability are allowed inputs.
Hidden identity, frozen rite outcome and source-support draw are excluded.
Matching AI inputs with different hidden draws must produce identical choice weights.
Troop feasibility must use an approved visible condition or actual observed presence, without assuming future orders or enemy intentions.

### Persecution reaction

The corrected S1 formula is R = min(0.75, base backing chance + 0.15 × hostile occupation).

Backing is public, so a player's policy of persecuting only visitors with limited backing would not have the population-average reaction rate.
The applicable rate for that selected group would be 25 or 40 percent.

Neither reaction nor its absence identifies supernatural truth.
Reaction is a political consequence with one draw and a bounded local effect.
It does not branch on hidden identity.
The removed cooperation modifier is recorded as a resolved finding, not a current defect.

The corrected S3 order first applies the paid false-alarm cooperation loss, then checks whether the resulting cooperation is below 35.
A 40 to 30 transition qualifies.
A 45 to 35 transition does not.
Only a fully prepared false natural warning can then receive its one 20 percent reaction draw.
Limited preparation, an unpaid dismissal, a void source and preserved military control do not enter that panic pool.

Twenty percent is conditional on those gates.
It is not the rate of panic per issued vision.
The number of qualifying false alarms and their correlations remain campaign inputs.

The 30-day minimum is a future safety clamp and is unreachable under the three current multipliers.

The final boundary rules make the timing gates explicit.
An advanced source date immediately rechecks the one-day margin, and an unready response cannot receive retrospective protection.
Missing source receipts close as unobservable seven days after the danger-window end.
A later receipt can correct factual history but cannot reopen payment, achievements or Chaos awards.

Assuming the owner supplies nonnegative B and D, C is nonnegative and never exceeds D.
The final request D − C never exceeds D.
When D is at least 0.25B, the final request is at least 0.25B.
When the owner has already reduced D below that floor, Shaman adds zero and preserves the stronger owner result.

| Existing residual D/B | Limited final request/B | Full final request/B | Interpretation |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1.00 | 0.90 | 0.75 | A 10% or 25% reduction of the remaining request |
| 0.50 | 0.45 | 0.375 | Additional reduction applies to the residual |
| 0.30 | 0.27 | 0.25 | Full reaches the combined 75% mitigation limit |
| 0.25 | 0.25 | 0.25 | No remaining Shaman headroom |
| 0.20 | 0.20 | 0.20 | Stronger existing owner mitigation is preserved |

The full-rate cap starts binding below D/B = 1/3.
The limited-rate cap starts binding below D/B = 5/18.
These are exact policy breakpoints.
The formula never proves actual lives saved or damage prevented in another timeline.
Achievement and cooperation attribution still need the same transaction's owner result and positive accepted contribution.

The added active-disaster-relief mode does not alter any random weights.
Its three, two or one work-unit contributions are clamped by the remaining shortfall, so actual accepted work can be lower.
No expected rescue completion rate follows without the card's current phase, outstanding objective and remaining owner work.

## Chaos bounds and repetition

The award flags give a safe gross upper bound of +12 for a welcomed encounter.
The largest initial-rite award is +6, the matching-natural milestone is +4 once, and the panic milestone is +2 once.
Exceptional and adverse initial-rite awards cannot both be obtained from the single rite.
Persecution closes the relationship and cannot be added to the welcomed path.
Its separate gross upper bound is +2.

The two distinct containment flags give a loose total deduction bound of −2, with the additional rule that the encounter's cumulative net contribution cannot fall below zero.
Those deductions require actual remaining event-owned burdens and the corresponding prior positive attribution.
They are not automatic refunds for clicking a recovery action.
The third vision, multiple credit installments, repeated result views and save reloads cannot reset any Chaos milestone flag.

The current unextended panic lasts fourteen days and reconciliation also needs fourteen days of work.
Even immediate reconciliation cannot finish with positive panic duration remaining under exact elapsed-day arithmetic.
The amended S3 correctly permits cooperation repair after expiry and forbids a negative Chaos award for that expired burden.
The −2 figure therefore remains a conservative flag-level ceiling rather than a claim that two deductions are attainable on the present timed path.

The +12 bound is conservative.
If exceptional delivery and its +15 cooperation always settle before any vision resolves, the occupied welcome minimum becomes 55.
Two paid false alarms then leave 35, which is not strained, so an exceptional rite, a matching-natural award and panic cannot all fit within three visions on that ordering.
The corresponding immediate-settlement maximum would be +10.

The design also permits deferred reserve credit and medical readiness.
Final S2 now gives each rite one cooperation-settlement receipt.
It settles at the first actual useful delivery using the applicable delivered class, or neutrally at final expiry if no delivery occurs.
It cannot charge an initial inconclusive penalty and later grant a second exceptional cooperation reward for the same rite.
A possible policy trace is occupied welcome at 40, a pending exceptional delivery, a full false alarm taking cooperation to 30 with panic, a later real exceptional delivery, and a later matching natural consequence.
That trace illustrates why deferred delivery must be considered, without claiming its realized probability or proving a particular campaign's timing feasible.
Accordingly, +10 must not be advertised as the unconditional campaign maximum.
Final S5 explicitly retains +12 as the conservative gross envelope.
The one-settlement ambiguity is resolved, while attainability of the upper envelope remains dependent on owner delivery timing and actual consequences.

The final S2 payment and expiry changes preserve those bounds.
Dispatched and held equipment balances are allocated separately across selected states with frozen integer remainders.
Loss of a military focus cancels its entire package, while a lost supporting state refunds only its exact held allocation.
An extinct original payer forfeits any remaining refund, so a successor cannot inherit a second entitlement.
Medical recurrence can consume readiness only within the original 30-day window and cannot restart a longer protection period.
None of these lifecycle clarifications changes a probability-bearing weight.

Every positive award still requires actual delivery or a matching owner consequence.
An exceptional draw with no delivery yields no manifestation award.
An adverse draw with no applicable harm yields no adverse award.
Final S2 explicitly makes an adverse food draw at zero reserves neutral wasted work.
It creates no harmful modifier, cooperation change or Chaos award.
Its adverse food row now describes one measured spoilage transaction, with no unspecified 30-day penalty.
This resolves the remaining consequence ambiguity without changing the outcome draw or any calculated fixture.
A persecution reaction with no valid local consequence yields no award.
Source support alone yields no vision award, and a false warning without actual panic yields none.
The shared-source overlap rule can only reduce these event-owned maxima.

- Current doctrine objects use folders, grand doctrines, tracks and sub-doctrines. Scripted one-time activation `effect` blocks have no documented automatic undo. A modifier or equipment bonus with defined removal is a different mechanism.
- Native raid `success_levels` callbacks start in `RAID_INSTANCE` scope. Actor and victim effect headings are not country-scope switches. Enter `var:actor_country`, `var:victim_country` or `var:target_state` explicitly. Concurrent jobs must never share one pending scalar. Native equipment and Command Power payments must not be charged again in script.
- These are conditional engine constraints. Reading all skills does not require adding a focus tree, technology, raid, country package, custom GUI, custom unit or 3D model to a minor event.

### Source and art rules

- Grounded regional or cultural portrait subjects use attributed source-first production and fail closed when that route cannot be completed. A supernatural plot does not by itself change grounded subject classification.
- Portrait production and portrait-specific wiring belong to `chaosx_portrait_creator`. Non-portrait archival imagery belongs to `chaosx_asset_source_researcher`. Original fictional report scenes belong to `chaosx_generated_event_art`. Icons belong to `chaosx_icon_artist`.

- The generated icon worker cannot modify gameplay, GUI or GFX unless its narrow assignment explicitly changes that ownership. Custom unit counters require exact installed-vanilla definitions, DDS files and sampled green palette. Achievement art is a single subject with deterministic state derivation and the immutable template triplet.
- 3D work uses modern designed artwork, not archival or ethnographic sources. Its source gate rejects anime presentation and out-of-period ordinary equipment. Body and equipped items now use separate one-image geometry tasks. These strict 3D rules are not a reason to reclassify an archival 2D report image.

### Role and tool evidence

- Current supplied config declares the `hoi4_agent_tools` route, optional `hoi4-live` and `clausewitz_linux`, optional `meshy`, the bounded `blender_hoi4` adapter, an isolated `blender_lab_dev` authoring profile and `gptimage`. These are repository configuration evidence, not proof that this session exposes any of them. The supplied config's approval and sandbox declarations do not replace the actual session permissions.
- Current probability tools are `hoi4.probability_inspect` and `hoi4.probability_analyze`. Analyze modes include sweep, compare, simulate, sequence and render. Legacy separate evaluate/sweep/compare expectations need schema reconciliation. An unexposed tool must not be reported as executed.
- AI auditor results need exact, bounded, sampled, score-only or unresolved classification. A score race, willingness score, timing distribution and proportional random selection are different. Complete pools and external factors are required before exact selection probability claims.
- Current MCP failures are bounded by the shared retry limit. A verified source calculation is permitted where tooling cannot support the actual script, with the limitation stated. An unavailable old baseline does not justify comparing a file with itself.
- Current localisation auditor is patch-capable within assignment and must examine actual prose clarity, not just key existence. It preserves dynamic tokens, real attributed quotes, mechanical meaning and regional identity. It routes workbook changes to the spreadsheet owner.
- The event UI worker owns only a dedicated event mechanic window with explicit exact identifiers and an accepted reference. Shared log, event details, settings and super-event frameworks remain parent-owned. UI values and actions are bounded by the skill's density budget. Reading the role is not proof a new dedicated window is warranted.
- Save inspection is read-only and applies only to supplied or specifically needed runtime saves. It must not launch the game or edit user settings. A plain-text save proves only its own date, version and state. Runtime uncertainty can justify one concrete save request, but it is not a precondition for fixing a clear source defect.

## Additional version conflicts and precedence issues

- Legacy custom roles use `.agents/skills`, current role exports use `.claude/skills`.
- Legacy roles frequently make missing MCP render evidence a hard blocker. Current role exports and current root skills permit direct source work after bounded failures with honest limits. Resolve using the current project instructions, not the stricter stale prose by default.

- Current technology skill says `research_bonus` may be used in leader traits while current characters skill says `research_bonus` and `rule` do not work there. The installed trait documentation must settle an actual use. This is not relevant unless the design chooses that surface.
- Full current event catalog and scenario catalog are export snapshots. They may carry inconsistent older punctuation or numbering. New writing must follow the current prose rules and user intent. Catalog content does not override requested Event 118 identity, but the remap must be explicit and collision checked before implementation.

# Reader C source-ingestion findings

## Coverage and method

This is a source-reading handoff, not Shaman design or implementation.
The source gate remained closed throughout this work.
No external research or substantive design was performed.

The primary assignment contains 46 unique files, 936,833 source bytes and 930,491 decoded characters.
The supplemental assignment contains Reader A indices 30 through 44 and Reader B indices 35 through 44, another 25 unique files, 96,918 bytes and 96,251 decoded characters.
Together these are 71 unique assigned files, 1,033,751 bytes and 1,026,742 decoded characters, plus the project source protocol read first.
Every unique assigned file was read directly in bounded complete outputs.
No cross-reader or cross-version text-span reuse was used for these readings.
Byte-identical copies listed in the inventory were verified by SHA256.
One context-truncated primary emission was discarded before acknowledgment and the entire unread range was reread in smaller outputs.
There are no unread ranges, omissions, or source-reading simplifications in these assignments.

Coverage receipts are `source_review/reader_c_receipt.json` and `source_review/reader_c_supplement_receipt.json`.
Each includes source hashes, actual decoded character ranges and final status.
The supplement retains the original assignment owner and index.
All ranges were audited for gap-free coverage and every listed duplicate copy was rehashed.

The independent root/inventory audit is `source_review/reader_c_root_coverage_audit.json`.
It verifies all 151 unique inventory hashes, all 193 source paths, all five archives including nested archives, exactly one assignment per unique file, and no unassigned archive members.
All 15 root receipt coverage maps are gap-free and seven comparison maps have exact source/target text equality.
Actual root reuse depends only on Reader A's directly read legacy planning file, so that reuse has no cycle.
At audit time, 51 changed-span labels still said `requires_direct_read` despite their enclosing completed-read attestation.
Root updated those completion labels, and the final recheck found zero stale `requires_direct_read` modes.
This metadata audit verifies hashes and coverage relationships, while another reader's actual processing remains that named reader's attestation.

## Authority and scope constraints

The project source protocol requires full supplied-source ingestion before planning and an honest account of any missing content.
Current applicable owner skills and source contracts should govern implementation after the gate.
Legacy variants remain evidence of previous requirements and must not be treated as current merely because their wording is detailed.
User directions govern the proposed event identity and scope.
The protocol allows useful targeted repository inspection after the gate, and unavailable MCP/custom-agent infrastructure is a disclosed limitation rather than a reason to omit the plan.
No tool, live-game review, asset, or code implementation should be represented as completed by this source pass.

All supplied skill families were processed in the assigned sources, including long legacy and unrelated surface references.
Applying a skill means considering its scope and recording why a surface is applicable or absent, not inventing focus trees, countries, technologies, fleets, animations, or 3D units solely to exercise every skill.
Current improvement guidance explicitly rejects extra meters, shallow decisions, decorative GUI, and unnecessary route expansion as substitutes for meaningful play.

## Catalog identity and version differences

The legacy events CSV at `project_sources/19-chaos_redux_events_catalog-5-.csv` contains Shaman at catalog row ID 129.
Legacy catalog ID 118 is Plague of locust.
The user's Event ID 118 and Original catalog ID 129 must therefore remain a deliberate mapping, not an assumption that legacy row 118 already means Shaman.
The current event catalog should be reconciled by its owning reader before any runtime namespace or workbook update.

Legacy and current cluster exports materially differ.
For example, legacy Intelligence is cluster 8 and current Intelligence is 20, legacy Diseases is 13 and current Diseases is 8, legacy Random Stuff is 19 and current Random Stuff is 12, and Pacts moves from 12 to 13.
Membership and wording also change, including Event 29 and the treatment of Event 22.
These are version changes, not duplicate text.
Natural Disasters remains Event 013 and cluster 5 in the supplied exports, but that does not make its current lifecycle contract identical to an older description.

The authoritative catalog is `docs/spreadsheets/chaos_redux_events_catalog.xlsx`.
The three CSVs are export-only, and `.tools/export_event_catalog_csv.py` must run after any accepted workbook save.
Before actual workbook work, read `docs/spreadsheets/README.md`, inspect real headers and table ranges, and inspect exporter `SHEET_EXPORTS`, `SHEET_WIDTHS` and cache checks.
Preserve legitimate unavailable rows, cluster slot order and repeated memberships.
`Details` is complete premise prose, and evolution fields contain full implemented evolution descriptions rather than selector titles.
Status claims require implementation evidence, while `Playable` specifically requires explicit approval.
A specification alone is not implemented or playable status.

## Exact owner-document and source map

The paths in this table are named by fully read supplied sources.
They are repository follow-up targets, not a claim that the underlying live repository files have been inspected in this pass.

| Surface | Exact owner paths named in supplied sources | Proven contract and remaining question |

Event 013 owns validation, target resolution, delayed work, impact, reports, aftermath and cleanup. Supplied registry does not prove a future-disaster subscription or mitigation receipt API. Inspect owner document and actual lifecycle before defining a compatible foresight adapter. |

It can call `chaos_meter_register_deaths` with population mutation disabled to prevent a second debit. Caller initializes outputs before invoking. |

Exact modifier scope, duration, movement and beneficiary behavior must be verified from installed references and precedent. |

Do not invent a generic cure, global health decrement, hidden future queue or shared capacity contract from a catalog description. |

The disaster gateway requires `natural_disaster_call_*` temporary inputs and any documented regular event targets.
Outputs include `natural_disaster_call_result`, `_reject_reason`, `_sequence_id`, `_primary_job_count`, `_skipped_primary_count` and resolved-target proofs.
Invalid or incomplete input fails closed and queues no work.
The gateway clears public call inputs after use while preserving caller-readable results.

The exact loss helper accepts requested population, protected minimum, reason, log flag, target country, target-presence proof and one-shot supplied-contract flag.
It measures population before and after and logs only observed positive loss.
Disabled Deaths logging does not prevent the physical loss transaction.
Ordinary civilian effects exclude actual nonhuman countries through the central classifier.
`is_special_chaos_country` and `is_actual_nonhuman_country` have different meanings, so an unusual human country must not automatically be excluded as nonhuman.

## Runtime integrity requirements from supplied skills

Temporary outputs first created inside a scripted helper can disappear on return.
Every caller, including nested callers, must initialize consumed temporary outputs before calling the helper.
Normal variables and arrays retain owning scope, while temporary arrays are unscoped within the chain and must use the actual temporary-array commands.
Regular event targets are chain-lifetime pointers, not durable IDs, and nested calls can overwrite a shared name.
Async work therefore needs persisted actor/state/generation identity and live authority checks at resolution.

Use explicit success and consumption receipts tied to current context.
An old used or tombstoned marker does not prove a fresh consumption, and rollback may reverse only the exact consumption performed by this transaction.
Keep immutable provenance and original due dates across controller-change callbacks.
Callback frequency is not elapsed time.
Every nested loop owns its reset break variable, and sparse processors preserve unvisited or unacknowledged queue suffixes.
No new unscoped whole-world periodic scans are justified by a small event.

State pointers require state validation, not a country `exists` test.
Country `ROOT` does not rebind when entering another country's scope.
Native `on_state_control_changed` supplies ROOT as new controller, FROM as old controller and FROM.FROM as state.
Native `on_annex` supplies ROOT as winner and FROM as annexed country.
State ownership, control and population-system eligibility are separate facts.

Shared date helpers convert ordinary days to engine date-unit offsets.
Raw day counts must never be added to a stored date.
The supplied registry states one hour is 0.00001 and one day is 0.00024 in that representation.
Existing finite modifier expiries must be preserved on rebinding, and removing one modifier must not erase another family's registry entries.

Payments require a single inclusive affordability contract used by availability, cost text and AI.
Dynamic quotes must display the precision actually charged.
Native `custom_cost_text` requires base, blocked and tooltip localisation keys.
Inline costs show no more than three values with matching texticons, while the separate gameplay hard limit is no more than four spendable cost types.
Timed paid actions publish an actor/family/generation receipt before charging and do not charge again at expiry.
Cancellation and success cleanup must be idempotent.
Use actual recorded payment for refunds and account for native factory reservation without reserving it twice.
Production contract tests must execute real owner helpers rather than replace required mappers and receipts with no-ops.
Source tests do not prove engine timing.

## AI, military and presentation constraints

Event `ai_chance`, decision `ai_will_do`, focus AI races and MTTH timing are different mechanisms.
Decision willingness is not normalized selection probability.
An all-zero event-option weight set falls to the first option.
Probability claims need complete pools and declared external factors.
Exact, bounded, sampled, score-only and unresolved findings must remain separate.
Hidden oracle truth must not become an undeclared AI advantage.

The units skill says no effect creates, issues or cancels battle plans.
AI front strategies can influence existing fronts with verified selectors and priorities, but this does not create scripted troop routing.
Top-level unit `defense` and terrain-block `defence` use different spellings.
`add_unit_bonus` addresses sub-units/categories, and dynamic modifiers may be country-based.
None of this establishes a portable per-army local terrain enchantment without further scope evidence.

Event Details and spreadsheet Details describe the situation and premise, never a list of mechanical effects.
Descriptions drawn on light parchment use plain text rather than section-sign colors, including dynamic substitutions.
Options and supported dark tooltips can use their normal colored formatting.
Descriptions communicate in-world consequences and do not advertise achievement paths.
Integer concepts display integer values.
Public cost and consequence clarity can coexist with hidden future surprises.

A justified custom GUI needs a reference before implementation, real native controls, finite visible-value/action budgets, exact state/resolution review and an event UI handoff.
The dedicated event UI worker has no ownership of shared event logs, Event Details, settings, generic registries or super-event frameworks.
Simple description and decision presentation remains valid when it communicates the mechanic.
Category art is not automatically a custom control surface.
Formable state puzzles and geometry contracts apply only to actual formable territory proofs.

## Assets and optional surfaces

Report art is a processed 210 by 176 documentary card with transparent corners, subtle tilt and shadow, black-and-white sepia treatment.
News art is 397 by 153 black and white.
Super-event art is 457 by 328.
Exact consumer and current reference family govern final sizes and bindings.
Icons for focus, idea, decision, achievement and other surfaces require their own native treatment, and a resized icon from another family does not satisfy that requirement.
Alpha-backed generated assets request native transparency in the initial generation.
Animation requires real source frames, a static fallback and verified consumer support.

Every character portrait belongs to the portrait creator.
Grounded identities require attributed source research and retain their identity.
Fictional identities use native ImageGen with explicit source-mode and review records.
A sourced grounded placeholder is a distinct, disclosed status, and the user alone supplies a requested RunPod-styled final.
No one should start or operate RunPod as part of this task.

New countries, focus trees, custom units, technologies, fleets or world-end branches each carry large additional contracts if the accepted design actually needs them.
Existing countries retain meaningful existing trees unless an authorized transformation requires replacement.
Current unit-family registration points include `docs/testing/chaosx_test_country.md`, `docs/systems/cbrn_warfare/chaos_unit_family_registry.md`, and `docs/events/019_infantry_spawn/systems/unit_family_coverage.md`.
These obligations do not imply creating a new unit for a purely temporary troop advantage.
World-end branches require Chaos above 1000 and terminal framework integration, which is separate from an ordinary high-chaos evolution.
Manual triggerable scenarios have their own registry and setup contract and must not be mistaken for automatic event pacing.

## Supplied roles and tool names

Current supplied role files use names such as `chaosx-repo-explorer`, `chaosx-documentation-curator`, `chaosx-event-ui-worker`, `chaosx-map-states-worker`, `chaosx-equipment-units-worker`, `chaosx-technology-tree-worker`, `chaosx-focus-tree-auditor`, `chaosx-generated-event-art`, `chaosx-asset-source-researcher`, `chaosx-portrait-creator`, `chaosx-super-event-text-researcher`, `chaosx-super-event-audio-researcher` and `chaosx-spreadsheet-doc-worker`.

Do not claim a custom agent runtime or unavailable model was launched merely because its definition was read.
Project role prompts must be self-contained and use no inherited parent context when newly spawned as project custom subagents.

## Next source work after the full team gate

Check current catalog and runtime numbering together.
